nina_r: short thread - roadmap decision: default quota model for reserved pools. options: per-tenant soft quota (best-effort spill) vs strict per-tenant hard quota (reject when exceeded). customers asking for predictability and fairness.
samk: soft quota = better overall utilization, fewer rejects, but noisy neighbors can steal capacity during bursts.
eric_dev: hard quota = clearer SLAs but increases wasted headroom and complicates autoscale fallback.
maya_ops: ops angle: hard quota simplifies preemption logic and incident reasoning. We've had a few incidents where soft spillover caused tail latency for high-priority tenants.
billing_bot: note: hard quota may require contract language updates for some tiers.
nina_r: proposal: hybrid default: soft quota with an opt-in "hard reservation" tier. provide eviction priority matrix and guarantees for hard tier.
samk: need to define admission controls and observable signals: quota_enforce_mode, current_spill, preempt_count.
eric_dev: implementation: runtime flag quota_mode per-pool + preempt policy that prefers soft-tenants when capacity constrained.
maya_ops: rollout plan: 1) add quota_mode flag behind feature flag 2) test in canary region 3) add billing + contract templates for hard tier.
nina_r: launch criteria: canary run with 10 tenants for 72h, preemption_count < 5/day, customer-reported fairness score > 8/10.
samk: timeline: can we ship feature flag + runtime changes in 3 sprints? I'll scope minimal viable controls.
eric_dev: yes, can do basic enforcement and metrics in that window.
maya_ops: ops will draft runbook and SLA language.
nina_r: owners: samk=eng, maya_ops=ops & contracts, eric_dev=runtime. I'll own product comms. Sync next week for status.
